beats.text: For two decades, the story was that walkers fell into step.
beats.note: Engineers described synchronous lateral footfall. In a big enough crowd, enough people stepped in unison by chance to feed the sway.

beats.text: Opened on 10 June 2000. Closed on 12 June.
beats.note: Opening day drew roughly 90,000 to 100,000 people, depending on the source, with up to 2,000 on the deck at once.
Douglas Taylor reports a lateral frequency band of 0.5 to 1.1 hertz, with accelerations of up to 0.25 g.

beats.text: In 2021, researchers said the stepping was not the cause.
beats.note: A team led by Georgia State University and the University of Bristol reported in Nature Communications that synchronised walking is typically a consequence of the bridge moving, not the cause.
Wikipedia says stiffening was rejected because it would greatly change the look of the bridge. Taylor reports 37 viscous dampers cut peak acceleration from 0.25 g to 0.006 g.

beats.context: About how long the bridge stayed shut, from 12 June 2000 to reopening on 22 February 2002.

beats.text: The fix worked. The explanation behind it may not have been the whole story.
